nodes.line: I know that look. Everyone wants something today.

Someone has to, and it may as well be you. The number three green at Moore Park has had a bald patch the shape of Tasmania since the Sunday after payday, and the committee thinks I am inventing it. I have got no proof, which is exactly why I am asking. Say nothing to anyone on the way.

You are the first person to stop all morning. They have seen the photograph and now they want it re-laid by the Sunday after payday, which means finding $53 that the Moore Park club does not have. It might be nothing. It has not felt like nothing. Do not make a scene about it.
Sit. Talk. Then I will decide how I feel.

choices.text: The Dead Patch at Moore Park — that's done.
Turf Money, Moore Park — that's done.

nodes.line: Fair enough. You know where I am.

npcs.name: Yasmin, club president at Moore Park

nodes.line: Give me a second. Right. Go.

Not being dramatic about this. Our books say 84 members at Moore Park and I would bet the bar takings that half of them are dead or moved to Queensland. I would not ask if there was anyone else about. Ask for me by name at the counter.

I am told you do odd jobs. Since two in the afternoon somebody has been going round the Moore Park greens telling the barefoot bowlers we are shutting, and we are not shutting. You can tell me I am imagining it. Tell me after. Come back and tell me straight.
You have got that look. Good or bad, out with it.

choices.text: The Moore Park Membership Count — that's done.
Closing Time Rumour, Moore Park — that's done.

nodes.line: Suit yourself. The offer does not go anywhere.

npcs.name: Raul, bar manager at Moore Park

nodes.line: You are not from around the corner, are you.

I'll be straight with you. There is a milk crate in the chest freezer behind the bar at Moore Park and I am not opening it on an empty stomach. I would have sorted it myself a year ago. Do that and we're square.

It has been three weeks. The man who kept these greens before me drinks at Surry Hills now, and he owes Moore Park an explanation about the drainage. It is not the money. It has stopped being the money. I will owe you one, and I pay those.
Before you start: did anyone see you.

choices.text: Behind the Bar at Moore Park — that's done.
The Old Greenkeeper, Moore Park — that's done.

nodes.line: No dramas. Come back when you are bored.

npcs.name: Tao, night console operator at Stanmore

nodes.line: Half of this suburb has walked past already. Not one stopped.

Someone has to, and it may as well be you. Every night around knock-off the same car does three laps of the Stanmore forecourt and never buys fuel. I have got no proof, which is exactly why I am asking. Say nothing to anyone on the way.

You are the first person to stop all morning. Now I know the plate, I want to know where it goes after it leaves Stanmore at knock-off, because it is not going home. It might be nothing. It has not felt like nothing. Do not make a scene about it.
Alright. I am listening properly this time.

choices.text: The Third Lap, Stanmore — that's done.

nodes.line: Suit yourself. The offer does not go anywhere.
Whatever it is, I have had worse this week.

Not being dramatic about this. Bay two at the Stanmore workshop has had the same car in it since grand final week and the owner has stopped answering. I would not ask if there was anyone else about. Ask for me by name at the counter.

I am told you do odd jobs. Someone has been walking out of Stanmore with a socket set at a time since grand final week, and I have run out of ways to be polite about it. You can tell me I am imagining it. Tell me after. Come back and tell me straight.
Say it plain and I will pay you plain.

choices.text: Tools Off the Bench, Stanmore — that's done.

nodes.line: No dramas. Come back when you are bored.
Sit down if you like. Nobody else is using it.

I'll be straight with you. Head office says the Stanmore board has been wrong since grand final week and I say it has been right for eleven years, and one of us is about to be embarrassed. I would have sorted it myself a year ago. Do that and we're square.

It has been three weeks. The bloke who runs the site at Lewisham has had the same trouble Stanmore has, and he will talk to you before he talks to me. It is not the money. It has stopped being the money. I will owe you one, and I pay those.
I had a feeling. Go on.

choices.text: The Stanmore Price Board — that's done.
The Other Franchise, Stanmore — that's done.

nodes.line: Right you are. Mind the step.
You will have to speak up, the trains are in.

Someone has to, and it may as well be you. Water has been coming through the level two ceiling of the Sutherland block since grand final week and the strata report says there is no water. I have got no proof, which is exactly why I am asking. Say nothing to anyone on the way.

You are the first person to stop all morning. The photo did it. It might be nothing. It has not felt like nothing. Now every owner at Sutherland owes $61 and I have to collect it from people who have avoided me for a year. Do not make a scene about it.
Take a breath. Then say the whole thing.

choices.text: The Special Levy, Sutherland — that's done.

nodes.line: No dramas. Come back when you are bored.
I have got about four minutes before I am needed.

Not being dramatic about this. Somebody who does not live at Sutherland has parked in space fourteen every night since grand final week and the manager will not look at it. I would not ask if there was anyone else about. Ask for me by name at the counter.

I am told you do odd jobs. The Sutherland AGM is on grand final week and I would like to arrive with something stronger than a grievance and a printout. You can tell me I am imagining it. Tell me after. Come back and tell me straight.
Go on then. What did you find.
Right you are. Mind the step.

npcs.name: Aisha, the one who does the bins at Sutherland

nodes.line: Ah. Someone with two working legs.

I'll be straight with you. Three units at Sutherland have put their bins out on the wrong night since grand final week and I have taken it personally, which I accept is a choice I made. I would have sorted it myself a year ago. Do that and we're square.

It has been three weeks. There is a block at Kirrawee with the same builder and the same cracks, and their manager has already been through what Sutherland is starting. It is not the money. It has stopped being the money. I will owe you one, and I pay those.
You came back. That already puts you ahead.

choices.text: Bin Night at Sutherland — that's done.
The Other Block, Sutherland — that's done.

nodes.line: Fair enough. You know where I am.
